html:
The Alexiad is a history of the reign of the Byzantine emperor Alexios I Komnenos, written around 1148 by his daughter Anna Komnene. It runs to fifteen books, in a learned, old-fashioned Greek modelled on the classical historians.

Anna wrote it in retirement after her failed bid for the throne, finishing a work begun by her late husband Nikephoros Bryennios. She is openly devoted to her father, but she used documents, letters and the memories of old soldiers, and the book is the main source for the empire from 1081 to 1118. It covers:

  • the wars with the Normans of Robert Guiscard and his son Bohemond
  • the Pecheneg wars and the victory at Levounion
  • the coming of the First Crusade, with vivid portraits of the Western knights, whom she found brave, greedy and rough
  • the Bogomil heretics and their trial in Constantinople

It is one of very few histories by a medieval woman, and one of the few Byzantine views of the crusades.
